AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Pest control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Pest control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Pest control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Pest control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Pest control.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structures in Animal production? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structures in Animal production.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structures in Animal production.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structures in Animal production.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structures in Animal production.

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 0 °C

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water conservation.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water conservation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water conservation.

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Vegetative propagation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Vegetative propagation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Vegetative propagation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Vegetative propagation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Vegetative propagation.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agroforestry? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agroforestry.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Agroforestry.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agroforestry.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agroforestry.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Production Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Production Structures.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Production Structures.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Production Structures.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Production Structures.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

13. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Digestive systems of animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Digestive systems of animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Digestive systems of animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Digestive systems of animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Digestive systems of animals.

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Vegetative propagation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Agroforestry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Protection: Pest control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Production Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Digestive systems of animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Parasite control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
